entities.summary: Quintus Poppaeus Secundus was a Roman consul suffectus in AD 9 and one of the authors of the lex Papia Poppaea, a comprehensive set of laws that reformed the Roman tax system and improved the lives of Roman citizens. He was a key figure in the Roman Senate and played a significant role in shaping the Roman Empire's governance. As consul, Poppaeus Secundus worked to strengthen the Roman economy and improve the welfare of its citizens. The lex Papia Poppaea, which he co-authored, had a lasting impact on Roman law and governance, influencing the development of Western legal systems. It is a testament to Poppaeus Secundus's enduring legacy that his laws continue to be studied and emulated by scholars and policymakers today. Poppaeus Secundus's remarkable achievements serve as a reminder of the power of effective governance and the importance of prioritizing the welfare of citizens.
